When indexing assets or records into a map/object by an ID, normalize the input collection using an array helper (e.g., `asArray`), filter out non-record entries, and ensure only entries with a non-empty ID string are indexed to prevent malformed or empty keys. Currently, `harnessRows` is iterated over directly without normalization, which can throw a TypeError if it is null or undefined.

When processing collections of assets or inputs, normalize the input using an array helper (e.g., `asArray`) and filter out non-record entries before mapping or flat-mapping over them to prevent TypeErrors on null, undefined, or non-array inputs. Currently, `row.locator_candidates` is mapped over directly without filtering out non-record entries first, which can cause a TypeError if any candidate is null or malformed.

```javascript
    candidate_pdf_page_indexes_zero_based: [...new Set(asArray(row.locator_candidates)
      .filter(isRecord)
      .map((candidate) => candidate.pdf_page_index_zero_based)
      .filter((index) => Number.isInteger(index)))].sort((left, right) => left - right),
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Ensure that threshold values are explicitly verified as valid finite numbers before performing numeric comparisons (such as `>=` or `<=`) in JavaScript. This prevents comparisons against `null` (which can occur when configuration files are missing or malformed) from erroneously evaluating to `true` due to null coercion to `0`.

```suggestion
  const coverage = Number.isFinite(summary.page_or_exact_coverage_ratio) ? summary.page_or_exact_coverage_ratio : 0;
  const threshold = Number.isFinite(COVERAGE_THRESHOLD) ? COVERAGE_THRESHOLD : 0.95;
  const gateBlocked = coverage < threshold;
```
